title: Runbook: Patroni failover for recon-pg
subtitle: Promote a replica, retarget ingest DSNs, verify WAL. Cluster recon-pg, etcd ns clh-etcd.
author: Aman Kumar
audience: On-call engineers, Diego Alvarez, Rina Das, Helen Cho, Priya Nair
owners: Rina Das (primary, DBA), Diego Alvarez (SRE), Aman Kumar (app DSN and ingest)
summary: This is the cold copy of the recon-pg failover procedure. Rina Das is primary. Engineers still need a copy they can follow at 02:00 without her on the call. Cluster name is recon-pg. DCS is etcd in namespace clh-etcd. We accept a 3 second async replication window, which is a known argument with Marcus Bell. The runbook covers planned switchover, unplanned promote, DSN updates on ingest and break-svc, WAL verification, and split brain. It also records the path we will not take: a same-quarter move to managed Multi-AZ as a substitute for knowing this procedure.
form_description: On-call runbook for Clearhaven recon Postgres. Written so a Northstar engineer can promote a replica, point ingest at the new primary, and confirm WAL without waiting for the DBA if Rina is unreachable.
revision_history: Draft from Diego's notes and the October 16 load-test replica lag scare.
Corrected etcd endpoints, added split-brain fencing, rejected sync replica.
DSN list for ingest, break-svc, match-engine. Commands against shadow.
Approved. Kept the 3s RPO. Marcus dissent recorded in section 8.

blocks.text: 1. If you only read one page

recon-pg is a two-node Patroni cluster. Primary today is recon-pg-01.chi.northstar.internal (10.8.14.21). Replica is recon-pg-02.chi.northstar.internal (10.8.14.22). etcd is three pods in ns clh-etcd. Apps do not connect to those hostnames. Apps connect to recon-pg-rw.clh.internal (primary) and recon-pg-ro.clh.internal (replica), which are Patroni-managed k8s Services. Failover is 'tell Patroni to switch, wait until rw points at the survivor, reload ingest DSNs if the pool still has the dead IP, verify WAL, then tell Helen.' If you cannot tell which node is primary, do not promote. That is how you get split brain.

blocks.label: RPO we will live with
blocks.text: Asynchronous streaming. We accept up to 3.0 seconds of committed-on-old-primary data loss on an unplanned failover. Marcus wants 0. Rina will not turn on synchronous_commit=remote_apply on this cluster because the October 16 11.4M run already pushed replica apply to 3.8 seconds and a sync replica would have stalled break-svc writes during the open. Priya signed the 3s window on November 8. If Marcus needs 0, that is a hardware and a latency conversation, not a toggle.

blocks.label: Do not
blocks.text: Do not promote both nodes. Do not pg_rewind a node that still thinks it is primary while apps are writing to it. Do not change ingest DSNs to a raw pod IP and walk away. Do not fail over during the 09:30-10:15 ET open unless the primary is actually dead. Do not 'just reboot the primary to see if it comes back' after Patroni has already promoted. That is split brain with extra steps.

Rina Das owns this cluster. Pager is #clh-dba and her cell on the on-call card. If she is on, she runs the failover and you run the app side (DSNs, consumer lag, Helen). If she is not on in 10 minutes, you run this document. Diego is backup for Patroni. I am backup for the DSN and ingest pieces. Kavya is backup for break-svc pools.
2. Preconditions. Check these before you touch Patroni.

items: Declare the incident in #clh-inc and page Helen Cho. If this is a planned switchover, skip the page and post in #clh-chg with the change id. Planned windows are Tuesday/Thursday 21:00-23:00 ET, never expiry Friday, never 09:00-10:30 ET.

Confirm you are talking to the shadow cluster or the prod cluster. Context: kubectl config current-context. Prod is clh-prod-use1. Shadow is clh-shadow-use1. Mixing them is how you fail over the wrong database.

Record current primary: kubectl -n clh-postgres get configmap recon-pg-leader -o yaml and curl -s http://recon-pg-01.chi.northstar.internal:8008/cluster | jq . Write the names down in the incident thread before you change anything.

Record replication lag: on the replica, SELECT EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp())); If this is over 15 seconds on an unplanned event, say so in the thread. Failover will lose more than 3 seconds. Marcus needs to hear that from us, not from a missing breaks row at 07:00.
Record ingest producer position: kafka-consumer-groups on clh.settlement.inbound and clh.match.inbound. Screenshot or paste. You will need it to see whether ingest stalled or just retried.

Confirm etcd is healthy: kubectl -n clh-etcd get pods and etcdctl --endpoints=https://clh-etcd-0.clh-etcd:2379 endpoint health. If etcd is the thing that is down, Patroni will not elect. Fixing etcd is a different runbook (Diego, CLH-RB-2024-003). Do not promote by hand to paper over dead etcd.

If this is planned switchover, drain match-engine and break-svc writes by pausing the k8s CronJob clh-file-lister and setting ingest replicas to 0 for 30 seconds. If this is unplanned, skip drain. The primary is already gone.

Two leaders: split brain, go to section 7. Zero leaders: etcd or both nodes down, call Diego.

If > 60 s, do not planned-switch. Unplanned: proceed but announce loss window.

If under 18%, promoting will fill WAL and die. Call Rina.
kubectl -n clh-prod get secret clh-ingest-dsn -o jsonpath
If it is already a pod IP, someone already panicked. Leave it until after promote, then fix.

blocks.text: 3. Planned switchover (primary is alive, we want the other node)

Use this for patching, for the November hardware window, for anything where recon-pg-01 can still accept a Patroni command. Planned switchover keeps the 3 second window near zero because the old primary flushes before it demotes. This is the path we practiced on shadow October 29.
3.1 Switch

# from laptop with prod kube context, or from jump-01.chi.northstar.internal
export PGHOST_VIP=recon-pg-rw.clh.internal
# who is leader
curl -s http://recon-pg-01.chi.northstar.internal:8008/cluster | jq '.members[] | {name,role,host}'
# scheduled switchover, Patroni picks the replica
curl -s http://recon-pg-01.chi.northstar.internal:8008/switchover -XPOST -d \
  '{"leader":"recon-pg-01","candidate":"recon-pg-02"}'
# watch
watch -n 2 'curl -s http://recon-pg-02.chi.northstar.internal:8008/cluster | jq .scope,.members'
blocks.caption: Planned switchover against current names. If the leader is already recon-pg-02, swap the names. Do not copy this blindly from the last ticket.

items: Wait until GET /cluster shows recon-pg-02 as leader and recon-pg-01 as replica. Usual time on shadow was 4.6 to 7.2 seconds. If it sits more than 30 seconds, stop. Do not fire a second switchover.

Confirm the Service: kubectl -n clh-postgres get endpoints recon-pg-rw. Address must be 10.8.14.22 after this example switch. If it still shows .21, Patroni REST succeeded and k8s Endpoints did not. Go to section 6.

Reconnect check from ingest: kubectl -n clh-prod exec deploy/clh-ingest -- psql "$DSN" -c 'select pg_is_in_recovery(), inet_server_addr();' pg_is_in_recovery must be f. inet_server_addr must be the new primary.
Unpause ingest if you scaled it to 0. Confirm produce to clh.match.inbound resumes. Lag should be flat, not climbing.

Ask Rina, or yourself if she is off, to run CHECKPOINT on the new primary and confirm the old primary is streaming. pg_stat_replication on the new primary should show recon-pg-01 in streaming, flush_lag under 1 second.
Post the before/after leader names, the endpoints IP, and the lag number in #clh-chg. Close the change.

blocks.text: 3.2 If switchover refuses

Patroni will refuse if the replica is too far behind (our maximum_lag_on_failover is 1048576 bytes, 1 MiB) or if etcd cannot take the lock. Refusal looks like HTTP 412 or a JSON body with 'failed to switchover'. Do not then ssh to the replica and pg_ctl promote. That bypasses fencing. Fix lag or fix etcd, then retry once. Second refusal: stop and call Diego. We have a leftover ssh promote in an old gist from 2022. That gist is why this runbook exists. Ignore the gist.
4. Unplanned failover (primary is dead)

Dead means: Patroni REST on the primary does not answer for 20 seconds, ssh does not answer, and kubelet says the node or the pod is NotReady. Slow primary (CPU 98 percent, still answering :8008) is not dead. Slow primary during the 09:32 open is the load-test problem, not this runbook. Do not fail over a slow primary at the open. You will lose writes and you will not gain a faster box, because the replica has been applying the same work.
4.1 Let Patroni elect, then verify

ttl is 20 seconds, loop_wait 10. A dead primary should stop being leader in about 30-40 seconds without you. Watch /cluster. The replica should become leader by itself. Your job is to confirm it did, confirm apps followed the VIP, confirm WAL, and fence the old node so it cannot come back as a second primary.

# unplanned: do NOT call /switchover if the leader is already gone.
# watch election
curl -s http://recon-pg-02.chi.northstar.internal:8008/cluster | jq '.members[] | {name,role,state}'
# if replica is still replica after 45s and primary is gone, etcd may be partitioned.
# only then, and only if etcdctl shows this node can write:
curl -s http://recon-pg-02.chi.northstar.internal:8008/failover -XPOST -d \
  '{"leader":"recon-pg-01","candidate":"recon-pg-02"}'
# fence the old primary so it cannot accept writes if it wakes
ssh recon-pg-01.chi.northstar.internal 'sudo iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 5432 -j REJECT'
# Rina prefers Patroni rest /switchover with a dead leader; iptables is the extra belt.
blocks.caption: Unplanned promote. The iptables fence is mandatory if the old disk might come back. Remove the rule only after pg_rewind, never before.

items: Wait for recon-pg-02 (or whoever survived) to report leader and running.
Confirm endpoints recon-pg-rw. If kube did not update, patch the Endpoints object only if Rina or Diego is on the call with you. A wrong patch is split brain in YAML.

Bounce ingest, break-svc, and match-engine Hikari pools so they drop the dead IP. See section 5. Patroni VIP should make this a no-op. In practice we still see 8-12 connections hanging in TCP to the dead node.
WAL verify, section 6. Do this before you tell Helen 'we are back.'
Leave the iptables REJECT on the old node until rewind. Ticket the rewind as CLH-TCK-9118 follow-up if it is after hours. Do not rewind at the open.

blocks.text: 5. Update ingest DSNs and bounce pools

This is the app-side work Rina should not have to remember. Secret clh-ingest-dsn in ns clh-prod should already be postgres://clh_ingest@recon-pg-rw.clh.internal:5432/recon. break-svc and match-engine use the same host, different users (clh_break, clh_match). If someone set a pod IP during a previous fire, fix the secret back to the VIP before you bounce.

# show what we will connect to
kubectl -n clh-prod get secret clh-ingest-dsn -o jsonpath='{.data.dsn}' | base64 -d; echo
kubectl -n clh-prod get secret clh-break-dsn -o jsonpath='{.data.dsn}' | base64 -d; echo
# if host is not recon-pg-rw.clh.internal, reset it
# (example; do not paste a real password into Slack)
kubectl -n clh-prod create secret generic clh-ingest-dsn \
  --from-literal=dsn='postgres://clh_ingest:${PW}@recon-pg-rw.clh.internal:5432/recon' \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
# bounce pools: rolling restart, pdb maxUnavailable=1
kubectl -n clh-prod rollout restart deploy/clh-ingest deploy/break-svc deploy/match-engine
kubectl -n clh-prod rollout status deploy/clh-ingest --timeout=180s
# prove the new primary
kubectl -n clh-prod exec deploy/clh-ingest -- python -c \
  "import os,psycopg2; c=psycopg2.connect(os.environ['DSN']); cur=c.cursor(); \
   cur.execute('select pg_is_in_recovery(), inet_server_addr(), now()'); print(cur.fetchone())"
blocks.caption: DSN reset and pool bounce. PDB on these deploys is maxUnavailable=1 after the January rebalance incident. Do not scale them to 0 on an unplanned failover unless ingest is already wedged.

blocks.text: Hikari connectionTimeout is 2.5 seconds on break-svc, 5 seconds on ingest. After a failover you will see a burst of connection failures in Datadog for 10-20 seconds. That is expected. A burst that lasts more than 90 seconds means the VIP still points at a dead IP or the new primary is rejecting (pg_hba, max_connections, or still in recovery). Do not keep bouncing. Check inet_server_addr.

rows: nothing. Read only. Points at recon-pg-ro.
blocks.caption: DSN inventory. ops-api must keep using the RO service. Pointing ops-api at rw during a failover is a habit from 2022. Stop doing it. Helen's terminals can live on a lagged replica.

blocks.text: 6. Verify WAL and that we are not in split brain
After every failover, planned or not, run this set. Paste the output into the incident thread. If any row in the check table fails, you are not done, even if HTTP 200 is back.

-- on the node you believe is primary, via recon-pg-rw
SELECT pg_is_in_recovery();                     -- must be false
SELECT inet_server_addr();                      -- must match kubectl endpoints recon-pg-rw
SELECT pg_walfile_name(pg_current_wal_lsn());   -- record this
SELECT client_addr, state, sent_lsn, replay_lsn,
       EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - replay_ts)) AS replay_lag_s
  FROM pg_stat_replication;                     -- 0 or 1 rows. If the old primary is fenced, 0 is OK.

-- on the replica (if it is up), via recon-pg-ro or ssh
SELECT pg_is_in_recovery();                     -- must be true
SELECT pg_last_wal_replay_lsn(), pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp();

-- timeline check, both nodes
SELECT timeline_id FROM pg_control_checkpoint();
-- if two primaries ever exist they will diverge timelines. same timeline_id + both
-- pg_is_in_recovery=false is split brain. go to section 7.
blocks.caption: WAL and timeline checks. timeline_id on prod as of November 8 is 14. After a real failover it will be 15. If you see 14 on one node and 15 on another and both think they are primary, that is the nightmare case.

rows: true: VIP still on a replica
Do not write. Fix Endpoints. Call Diego.
streaming or empty if old node fenced
one value cluster-wide among live writers
Cache cold + new primary IO. Wait 5 min. If not, this is a different incident.

blocks.text: 6.1 Endpoints did not move

We saw this on shadow October 29. Patroni REST said recon-pg-02 was leader. k8s Endpoints for recon-pg-rw still listed 10.8.14.21 for 38 seconds because the Patroni sidecar's callback to the Endpoints controller hung. Apps that already had connections were writing to the demoted node. That is a baby split brain. Fix: kubectl -n clh-postgres delete pod recon-pg-01-0 is the wrong fix. Right fix: kubectl -n clh-postgres get endpoints recon-pg-rw -o yaml, then if the address is stale and Patroni /cluster is clear, kubectl -n clh-postgres annotate endpoints recon-pg-rw clh.force-refresh=$(date +%s) does nothing useful. You have to patch the Endpoints subset addresses to the new primary IP, and you have to have Diego on the call. I am not putting the patch YAML in this runbook because a wrong copy-paste at 03:00 is worse than waiting 2 minutes for Diego. Page him.
7. Split brain

Split brain means two nodes both accepting writes. You will see it as: two pg_is_in_recovery()=false, different timeline_id, or ingest rows that exist on .21 and not on .22. Helen will see it as breaks that flip status, or match slices that complete then un-complete. Stop ingest before you think. Scale clh-ingest, break-svc writes, and match-engine to 0. ops-api can stay up on RO if RO is actually a replica. If RO is one of the two primaries, scale that too.

items: Scale writers to 0. kubectl -n clh-prod scale deploy/clh-ingest deploy/break-svc deploy/match-engine --replicas=0

Pick the surviving timeline. Default rule: the node that was already leader in etcd (kubectl -n clh-postgres get configmap recon-pg-leader) is the survivor. Exception: if that node has been down more than 2 minutes and the other node has the larger LSN and Helen confirms the writes she cares about are there, Rina can override. Engineers on the night shift do not override. You wait for Rina.
Fence the loser. iptables REJECT 5432, and systemctl stop patroni, in that order. Stopping Patroni first without fence can let a restart loop come back.

Do not pg_rewind until writers are at 0 and the loser is fenced. Rewind command is Rina's. Approximate form is pg_rewind --target-pgdata=/pgdata --source-server=... against the survivor. If rewind refuses, rebuild the loser from backup. That is a 40-70 minute restore on this dataset (1.84 TB as of November 6).
Only after rewind or rebuild: start Patroni on the loser, confirm it joins as replica, timeline matches, pg_stat_replication shows streaming.
Scale writers back, one deploy at a time, ingest first. Confirm health_probe INSERT. Then break-svc. Then match-engine.
Chris Patel will need a row-by-row gap report on ingest.raw_event for the loss window. Ticket it. Do not try to eyeball it from psql at 04:00.

blocks.label: Rejected: automatic pg_rewind in a sidecar
blocks.text: Diego proposed a sidecar that rewinds any node that loses leader. We rejected it on November 5. A rewind against a node that still has clients is data loss we cannot see. Split brain stays a human path with writers scaled to 0. The sidecar idea can come back when we have a third node and a witness. We do not have a third node.
I am not putting a rewind in a container restart loop on a clearing database. We talk through it or we restore.
8. The 3 second window, and Marcus

synchronous_commit on recon-pg is on (local flush). synchronous_standby_names is empty. That is async streaming. On a hard primary death, any transaction that committed on the primary and had not yet been flushed on the replica is gone. Rina measured p99 flush_lag at 0.84 seconds on a median day and 2.6 seconds on the October 16 11.4M open, with a 3.8 second poke. We wrote 3.0 seconds into this runbook as the number we tell Marcus, knowing the load-test poke went over. Priya accepted the gap. Marcus did not.

Marcus's position, said in the November 6 TAM call: a clearing affiliate cannot shrug at lost breaks. He wants synchronous_commit=remote_apply, or at least remote_write. Rina's position: remote_apply on this hardware turns a replica hitch into a primary stall, and break-svc at 11.4M already sits on PK lookups. A stall at 09:32 is a 40-minute match window with all the data 'safe' and none of it matched. Helen's position: she would rather replay 3 seconds of inbound Kafka (we still have the topic, retention 3 days) than freeze the primary. I agree with Helen and Rina. The inbound topic is the real log. Postgres is the derived state. We rebuild derived state. We do not freeze the open.

What we will do instead of sync replica this quarter: keep Kafka retention at 3 days (already paid for), keep the ingest idempotency keys so a replay does not double-write, and add a post-failover job that compares max(event_id) in ingest.raw_event to the Kafka high water mark on clh.match.inbound and clh.settlement.inbound. Chris owns that job design. Ticket CLH-TCK-9104. ETA December 4. Until that job exists, the comparison is manual and it is in section 6's INSERT probe plus a kafka-run-class GetOffsetShell. Ugly. Better than sync commit on this box.

blocks.text: 8.1 Rejected: lift to RDS Multi-AZ this quarter

Marcus asked whether we should stop running Patroni and buy Multi-AZ. Short answer: no, not as a failover strategy for recon-pg in Q4. The cluster is 1.84 TB, we use INCLUDE indexes that we just added after the load test, we use Patroni REST from this runbook, and we have etcd already. A Multi-AZ move is a migration project with a cutover weekend, a new DSN shape, a new backup tool, and a failover we cannot step through with curl. It does not remove the 3 second argument. It hides it. Rina also does not have RDS superuser for the things she does on rewind. We stay on Patroni. If Northstar ever wants managed Postgres, that is a 2026 conversation with a design doc, not a line in a runbook.
9. Commands that are easy to get wrong

items: pg_ctl promote on a replica while Patroni is alive: Patroni will fight you. Use REST /failover, not pg_ctl.

DROP replication slot on the old primary after switchover: only after the old primary is replica and streaming. Slot names are recon_pg_01 and recon_pg_02. Wrong drop breaks WAL recycle and fills disk in 2-6 hours at our WAL rate.
SELECT pg_wal_replay_resume() on a paused replica: we pause replicas for the schema SOP. If you failover a paused replica you get a leader that does not apply. Check pg_is_wal_replay_paused() first.
Changing max_connections during failover: no. That needs a restart. You do not have a restart budget at 02:00.
Pointing break-svc at recon-pg-ro because 'it is healthier': RO is a replica. break-svc writes. It will fail with read-only errors and it will look like a failover bug.
Running this runbook against clh-shadow-use1 by accident while prod is on fire: check context. Twice.

blocks.text:
# post-failover Kafka vs Postgres gap, manual version of CLH-TCK-9104
kafka-run-class.sh kafka.tools.GetOffsetShell \
  --broker-list kafka-prod-01.chi.northstar.internal:9092 \
  --topic clh.match.inbound --time -1
kubectl -n clh-prod exec deploy/clh-ingest -- psql "$DSN" -c \
  "SELECT source_topic, max(source_offset) FROM ingest.raw_event
    WHERE source_topic='clh.match.inbound' GROUP BY 1;"
# if Kafka high water is more than a few thousand ahead of max(source_offset)
# after drain, we lost ingest rows. Replay from the gap. Do not INSERT fakes.
blocks.caption: Gap check. Offsets are per partition; the SQL above is simplified. Chris has the per-partition query in clh-ingest/sql/gap_after_failover.sql. Use that if you have more than 2 minutes.

blocks.text: 10. Aftercare

items: Leave the fence on the old primary until rewind completes. A 'helpful' reboot from the cloud console is how the second primary returns.

File CLH-TCK-9118 for rewind if you did not already. Owner Rina. If she is off, Diego starts the restore from last night's basebackup plus WAL. Basebackup is in s3://clh-pg-backup/recon-pg/. Restore SOP is Rina's, not this document. Do not invent one.
Tell Helen the loss window in seconds, not 'we think we are fine.' Use the Kafka gap if you have it, else the replica lag you recorded in preconditions.
Watch break-svc PK p95 and match window for 60 minutes. Failover does not excuse an 11 minute match day. If lookup p95 stays high, this is now also a break-svc incident. Page Kavya.

Within 1 business day: post a 20-line note in #clh-inc with leader before/after, lag at decision, DSN bounce times, WAL timeline, and whether rewind or restore. Link this runbook. I will fold numbers back into v1.3 if anything was wrong.

If this was unplanned, Priya wants a 15-minute readout the next morning. You do not need a full incident report unless we lost more than 3 seconds or we hit split brain. If we hit split brain, we write a full incident. No debate.

blocks.text: I practiced the planned path on clh-prod-shadow on October 29 with Diego. Switchover took 6.1 seconds. Endpoints lagged 38 seconds that once, 4 seconds the second try. Unplanned path was injected by killing the primary VM for 90 seconds. Election 34 seconds, fence applied, rewind 11.4 minutes on the 420 GB shadow dataset (prod will be slower, 40-70 minutes, Rina's number). I did not practice split brain on shadow because we only have two nodes and inventing a second primary means a restore. That gap is real. If you hit split brain, you are in section 7 and you are waiting for Rina, and that is the correct amount of fear.
Version 1.2 is what Priya approved. If you change a timeout or a hostname, bump the version and tell me. A runbook that drifts from the cluster is how we get the 2022 gist again.
